title: emergency-comms-runbook-and-status-templates
summary: Practical runbook draft for SRE incident communications focused on fast, clear external status updates, customer-facing emails, and an internal war-room checklist. Designed to reduce cognitive load during high-severity incidents and provide copy+paste-ready templates for status.page, email, and Slack. Meant to complement the incident response checklist (see linked Confluence).
severity-defs:
sev0: service down / API returns 500s or >50% request error rate / major data loss; require immediate war-room.
sev1: degraded performance or partial feature outage impacting a subset of customers; war-room if impact widens.
sev2: intermittent errors or increased latency with mitigation available; handle via on-call + async comms.
sev3: informational (scheduled maintenance, low-impact bugs).
trigger-criteria: Trigger external comms when any of: sustained error rate >5% across production for 5+ minutes, latency p50 increases >2x baseline and p95 >4x baseline, customer-facing feature completely unavailable for >2 customers in a 10-minute window, or when Postmortem Owner deems customer notification appropriate. If in doubt, err on the side of transparency and post an initial holding message (Acknowledged) then update.
initial-actions_war-room-checklist:
1) Create war-room channel: #war-<incident>-<tz> in Slack and invite on-call + product + comms + account owner.
2) Triage owner: assign primary and secondary.
3) Snapshot: capture last 15 min logs, deployment diffs, recent config changes, recent infra alerts.
4) Customer scope: run quick query to list affected customers (by org_id/region).
5) Safety: if rollout/config change in last 60 minutes, pin rollback play ready.
6) External holding message: post initial status page update and short public Slack/X thread (see templates).
7) Notify legal/PR if data exposure is suspected.
8) Start timeline doc (chronology) in the war-room channel.
Notes: keep updates short, include ETA if known, prefer frequent cadence over long silence.
roles_and_responsibilities:
Incident Commander: overall coordination and when to escalate external comms.
Communications Lead: drafts + approves external messages and syncs with product/CS.
SRE Lead: technical triage and mitigation.
Customer Success Rep: identifies high-touch customers and preps targeted messages.
Legal/Privacy: reviews wording for data exposure.
Postmortem Owner: drafts RCA and actions within 72 hours.
All roles must document actions in incident timeline and annotate decisions and rollbacks.
external-comm-templates:
A) Status Page - initial (holding):
Title: "Service Disruption - Investigating"
Body: We are currently investigating an issue affecting the Redwood Inference API. Some requests may return errors or be delayed. Our engineering team is actively investigating. We will post updates every 15 minutes. Affected services: text generation API, embeddings (if known). Incident ID: {INCIDENT_ID}.
ETA: investigating.
---
B) Status Page - update (interim):
Title: {INCIDENT_ID} - Partial Mitigation in progress
Body: We have identified a likely root cause (brief, non-technical): e.g., a configuration rollback caused worker misrouting. We are applying a mitigation that should restore 80% of traffic within ~20 minutes. Impacted customers: {list or count}. Next update: {ETA or time}.
---
C) Status Page - resolved:
Title: {INCIDENT_ID} - Resolved
Body: The issue has been resolved and normal service restored at {TIME}. Cause: {short cause}. Customer impact: {summary}. Remediation: {what changed}. Follow-up: A post-incident report will be published within 72 hours.
---
D) Customer email (high-touch):
Subject: Incident {INCIDENT_ID} — Partial outage affecting Redwood API
Hi {Customer Name},
We wanted to let you know we encountered an outage that affected the Redwood API between {start} and {end}. Our teams prioritized mitigation and service was restored at {time}. During the window, {describe impact specific to them}. Root cause: {short statement if known}.
We apologize for the disruption. The engineering team is preparing a full post-incident report and will follow up with any specific customer actions (rate-limit resets, credits) if applicable. If you need immediate help, reply to this message or contact your CS rep {name/contact}.
Regards,
Asha Patel (on behalf of SRE & Product)
---
E) In-product banner (short):
We’re investigating a disruption affecting the API. See status.redwood.ai for updates.
---
F) Slack public-facing short blurb for community:#status
We’re investigating increased errors for the API. Engineers are on it. Updates on status.redwood.ai - Incident {INCIDENT_ID}.
internal_comm_cadence:
- Initial holding message: within 10 minutes of detection.
- Interim updates: every 15 minutes for sev0; every 30 minutes for sev1 until stabilized.
- If mitigation ETA > 1 hour, include estimated milestones: detection -> mitigation start -> mitigation complete -> verification.
- Final update/resolution: within 10 minutes of verification and then reminder when postmortem is scheduled.
- Postmortem status update: within 72 hours publish draft RCA to Confluence and circulate to execs + affected customers list.
escalation_policy:
- If incident persists beyond 30 minutes with no clear mitigation, escalate to Eng Director and Head of Product.
- If top-tier customer is impacted (SLA customer) escalate immediately to CS director for direct outreach.
- If data exposure suspected, call Legal + Security immediately and pause outbound customer messages until legal review provides guidance (but still post holding message about investigation).
post_incident_actions:
1) Create postmortem doc with timeline, root cause hypothesis, and corrective actions within 72 hours.
2) Assign action owners with due dates (no more than 30 days to remediate).
3) Share postmortem with execs and affected customers; schedule a 30-min go/no-go review if proposed infra/config changes are risky.
4) Runbook updates: capture lessons learned and update this runbook (owners: SRE lead + Comms).
5) Retro: schedule 60-min retro with all participants within 7 days.
6) Consider offering customer credits or targeted support if impact breaches SLA thresholds.
notes_to_self:
- Template language should be approved by comms/legal in quiet hours. Keep multiple approved variants ready for copy/paste.
- Consider adding short machine-readable incident tags to status page (component: api, region: us-east-1).
- Short-term: create Google Sheets query to surface list of affected org_ids by error code.
- Unresolved: define exact thresholds for 'affected customer' for automated CS ping.
- Add a lightweight webhook to notify CS slack channel when status page moves to "investigating" or worse.
